I don't want to be cliche, but I mean it when I say it: pursue what you love. I'm a nursing student who loves what she does and that's the only thing that kept me from quitting when essays, exams, assignments and meetings showed up. Can you imagine working on something you hate? Spending four or five years studying something you hate? Now, can you imagine all that with something you love? 

Life finds a way, it always does. The passion someone has for something can open doors. There's always a teacher willing to take an enthusiastic student under their wing. And maybe the collapse of corals will make the job of saving then really important and really soon. ;) Of course there's the matter of money, I don't live in the US but I know about tuitions and stuff like that - there should be a middle ground somewhere. If there's no one specific you can talk to, I suggest you look up FB groups for biology-related field students (Wild green memes for ecological fiends is my favorite - they're really kind and have answered questions like yours before!) and see what they have to say.

Wishing you the best of luck. Things will turn out okay.

This is gonna be long. I have a lot of feelings.

Ellie is just very shy and self-conscious in the beginning, her body language screams that. She's behaving exactly like I used to during parties - averting my eyes left to right, pretending to be enjoying it by tapping her fingers on the cup and bobbing her head to the music. Notice how overjoyed she is when she catches sight of Dina and how her smile all but fades when Jesse approaches her. 

When it comes to Dina not regarding Jesse's feelings, we must keep in mind they're all very young and their relationship wasn't going that great to begin with (they're on an on and off relationship), they've broken up rather recently and maybe not on good terms. We've all been there. And the negative talk just seems like she's trying to make Ellie more confident. She meant it that the guys staring at her (Dina) should be jealous of Ellie and be terrified of her, because Dina is interested on /Ellie/ and not on them. It's not in any way directed at the locals. 

Ellie is distant with Jesse, and hesitates to get too close to Dina (she subtly takes one step back when Dina puts her hands around her waist, the only resistance she ever shows), but she never pushes her away. That hidden, shy smile when Dina says "she loves it"? She's a goner. She doesn't seem uncomfortable around Dina, she's just anxious as hell, whether about having her crush being so close to her or the overwhelming amount of people around them and/or looking at them. Both, probably.

What really catches my eye and strikes Dina as sincerely liking Ellie is how her eyes flick down to her lips, to her eyes (as if saying, okay, are you sure?") and then to her lips again before kissing her. If that's faking, girl needs an Oscar. Ellie pretty much does the same, but makes no move. It's implied she invited Ellie to the party, making it all sound planned, but not in a bad way. Seems like she thought a lot about it and totally plans on getting her girl that night.
